title: Sharp Stage Compression, Universal 5-Prime Witness Optimality, and Exact Per-Job Cut Thresholds for Pinwheel Scheduling PSPACE-Completeness
abstract: Fotakis, Kanellopoulos, Mitropoulos, Pagourtzis, Papadimitriou, Pergaminelis, and Tolias (arXiv:2611.34869v1) recently settled the 37-year-old open problem of Holte, Mok, Rosier, Tulchinsky, and Varvel (1989) by proving that Pinwheel Scheduling with binary deadlines is PSPACE-complete via a three-stage reduction: Periodic 3-SAT -> Daily Scheduling with Breaks (Stage 1) -> Daily Scheduling (Stage 2) -> Pinwheel Scheduling (Stage 3). We establish sharp structural optimality and quantitative compression across all three stages. First (Theorem 1), in Stage 1 we prove that strip high hour H = 5 and inter-region gap g = 3 are exact minimums (with executable counterexamples at H = 4 and g = 2), compressing daily width from w = 72N + 15 to w = 60N + 13 (a 16.7% linear reduction cascading as (5/6)^4 = 625/1296 approx 0.482 into the Stage-2 O((Mw)^4 log^2(Mw)) job count), and construct an optimal 4-day (1-neutral-block) write phase offering relative offsets ({1,2}, {2,4}, {0,3}, {0,4}) between boundary ordinary days {0,5}, cutting write-phase overhead by 75% (M = 8m + 32 -> 8m + 8) and proving the unconditional lower bound L >= 4 days across all write calendars at H = 5. Second (Theorem 2), in Stage 2 we prove a universal combinatorial number-theoretic lower bound: any pairwise-coprimality two-hour witness gadget (c_1,...,c_r) of arbitrary size r (even allowing arbitrary prime powers) whose coprimality graph satisfies chi(G) >= 3 and omega(G) <= 2 contains an induced odd cycle C_{2s+1} (s >= 2) whose (2s+1)(s-1) non-edges require at least ceil((2s+1)(s-1)/C(s,2)) = 5 distinct primes, proving K = lcm(c_v) >= 2*3*5*7*11 = 2310 unconditionally; moreover, solving the exact filler-minimization problem at K = 2310 proves that (6, 10, 55, 77, 21) (in complement-cycle C_5-bar order) with CRT phases (4, 5, 11, 56, 15) is the unique global optimum (798/2310 witness density, 3822 rigid fillers versus Fotakis et al.'s rank-9/12 tuple (14, 33, 10, 21, 55) with 4002 fillers, saving 180 rigid jobs per two-hour test). Third (Theorem 3), in Stage 3 we sharpen the density-slack and expected-deviation bounds from n*Delta to the moving-job weighted rate S_2 = sum_{delta_i > 0} delta_i / b_i^2 (since rigid jobs contribute identically zero) and prove an exact per-job total-variation cut theorem reducing the soundness day-length threshold from T > n(2E + 3) to the single-slot-tight bound T >= E + 1 (saving > 2n in the cut step alone and Omega(n^2 / w_mov) overall). All 18 core algebraic theorems are formally verified in constructive Lean 4.35.0 (0 sorry, 0 Classical.choice, 0 custom axioms), backed by 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates and 56 adversarial tests.
